B: Alright.
A: Hi. Greta. Peterborough.
B: Dean. Gillingham.
A: Okay. Erm. So how was your first call?
B: Yeah, fine. Woman from London, runs a shop. Talked about coffee mostly.
A: Mine was about coats and spider plants. Very deep.
B: Ha. Could be worse.
A: What do you do?
B: Admin at a plumbing supplies place. Invoices, phones. Not exciting. You?
A: Graphic design, for a print and signage company. Menus, leaflets, van wraps.
B: Oh, vans. We've got loads of trade lads come in with them wraps on. Their name, a big tap or whatever. Some of 'em look a right state.
A: Yes! Thank you. Most of them are terrible. Too many colours, the phone number in five different fonts, a photo of a boiler from 2004. And they are so proud of it.
B: There's one bloke, Dave, his van's got his face on the side. Massive. Grinning.
A: His face? Oh no.
B: Proper. Everyone takes the mick. He loves it though, reckons he gets work off it.
A: That's the worst part. Probably he does. The ugly ones work. People trust ugly. It's very depressing for me, to be honest.
B: Ha. Didn't think I'd be talking about van fonts today.
A: Me neither. Sorry, it's my thing, I get a bit... Do you like your job?
B: Not really. It's alright. Part-time, pays the rent. That's it really.
A: Same, honestly. I want to go freelance, brand identities for cafés, breweries. I have half a portfolio. It's been half for two years.
B: Yeah. I've been saying I'll do an electrician course for about five years. So.
A: So we're both all talk.
B: Speak for yourself. Nah, you're right, fair enough.
A: My husband is an electrician. He says it's good money but his knees are destroyed.
B: That's what they all say. Still beats my desk, mind. Is it a lot of college?
A: I think a couple of years, and then you are somebody's... erm, what is the word, the helper.
B: Mate. Electrician's mate. Yeah, at thirty-three, carrying some bloke's bag about. Can't see it.
A: Thirty-three isn't old. I'm thirty-four.
B: Feels old some mornings. Neighbours were up till two, I'm knackered.
A: What do you do apart from work?
B: Football, FIFA, pub quiz. Normal stuff. You're gonna say art or something.
A: I am going to say art, yes. Lino prints. Behind me.
B: Oh, is that a fish?
A: It's a fish. Well done.
B: Alright, no need. It's good, to be fair. I couldn't do that.
A: Thanks. And my husband has football on every weekend, so I know the noise of it very well.
B: Who's he support?
A: Peterborough, and somebody red. I don't listen.
B: Red. Narrows it down to about nine teams.
A: Liverpool? I think Liverpool. He would be so upset I don't
